transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… good to meet you too. I guess I came in because things have felt a little… out of balance, maybe. I moved recently, and at first I was barely even getting settled into my new apartment, but then suddenly I started saying yes to all these mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and redoing my whole portfolio.

It’s not all bad, exactly—I mean, some of it is productive—but it felt like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint, if that makes sense. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it started feeling like more than just being motivated.
During this time, have you been needing less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I mean, a bit. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but for several nights I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours. And weirdly, I’d wake up feeling like I was totally fine—like I should use the extra time to get ahead on things. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that time, did you feel unusually confident in yourself or your abilities?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I felt more… capable, maybe? Like I could handle things if I just pushed through. But I don’t know if I’d call it unusually confident. Maybe more like I was trying to convince myself I had it together, if that makes sense.
During that period, were you talking more than usual?

Hmm… I’m not sure. I don’t think I was, like, obviously talking nonstop or anything. Maybe I was a little more eager in conversations, but I didn’t really notice myself talking more than usual. I guess I’d have to ask someone close to me to know for sure—does that make sense?
During that time, did you feel more driven than usual to start or do lots of projects or activities?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I tried to frame it as being productive, but it was kind of a lot. I’d barely even settled into my new apartment, and then suddenly I was saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and deciding I needed to redo my entire portfolio.

It felt like I had to fix everything in my life in one big sprint, if that makes sense. I know some of that sounds positive, and part of me was proud of it, but looking back it was more intense than my usual.
During that time, did this cause problems at work or in your relationships?

A little, yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like everything fell apart, because it didn’t exactly. But I did miss a design review at work, which was really unlike me and kind of embarrassing.

And I’ve been avoiding friends and family a bit, not because of them, just… I feel ashamed, I guess, about seeming so scattered and unreliable lately. I know that’s probably important to mention, right?
During that period, did you feel unusually irritable?

Yeah… a bit. I don’t want to make it sound like I was angry all the time, because I wasn’t, but earlier this month I felt almost… electric? Like really upbeat one minute, and then suddenly I’d snap at someone over something tiny.

I remember getting short with a contractor and also with my sister over small delays, like they were personally trying to get in my way. Which I know isn’t fair. I feel bad saying that, but yes, I was more irritable than usual.
About how many days in a row did that unusually energized and irritable period last?

Um… I guess it wasn’t just a few days. It’s been kind of this whole stretch since I moved into the apartment, so… about a month now.

Not every single moment was intense, but that up-and-down energized and irritable thing has been there on and off through that time, if that answers it okay.
During that energized and irritable period, did it ever get so severe that you couldn’t function normally at work or in daily life?

Not completely, I don’t think… like, I was still getting through most days, so I don’t want to overstate it.

But it did affect things. I missed a design review at work, which is really not like me, and I’ve been kind of avoiding friends and family because I feel embarrassed about how scattered and unreliable I’ve seemed lately. So… yeah, it wasn’t disabling exactly, but it wasn’t normal functioning either, if that makes sense.
During that energized period, did you have any hallucinations or delusional beliefs?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I wasn’t seeing things or hearing voices or anything like that.

And I don’t think I believed anything that wasn’t real. I was maybe overly confident or reactive, but not… out of touch with reality, if that’s what you mean. Does that answer it?
During that energized period, were you more physically restless or unable to sit still than usual?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I tried to frame it as being “productive,” but there were nights where I just could not sit still.

I’d be moving furniture around, labeling storage bins, tweaking design mockups, and then just pacing around the apartment because stopping felt… almost impossible. Not all night every night, but enough that it was definitely more than my usual. Is that the kind of restlessness you mean?
During that energized period, were you ever hospitalized because of it?

No, I wasn’t hospitalized for it. It never got to that point… thankfully. I mean, it was messy and not great, but I was still at home and getting by enough, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that energized period, did the symptoms cause marked impairment in your work or social life?

Um… not completely, but yeah, I think it did affect things more than I wanted to admit.

Work-wise, I missed a design review, which is… not like me, and I felt really embarrassed about that. And socially, I’ve kind of been avoiding friends and family because I feel like I’ve seemed so scattered and unreliable lately.

I don’t know if that counts as “marked,” but it definitely caused problems. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, or lost interest in almost everything?

I think… yes, lately it’s felt that way. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but I’ve been waking up with this heavy, gray feeling in my chest most days.

Even when the apartment is quiet and nothing especially bad is happening, I’ll feel like I could cry over something stupid, like a coffee mug left in the sink. I know that sounds small, but it’s been hard to shake. Is that what you mean by depressed most of the day?
During this recent low period, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still tell myself I want to do things, but when it comes down to it, there’s just no pull.

I used to really look forward to hiking at Crowders, or cooking something nice, or even just sketching interface ideas on my tablet for fun. Lately I’ll look at my hiking gear or open the tablet and just… stare at it. It doesn’t feel bad exactly, it just feels like nothing. Like the part of me that normally gets interested isn’t showing up.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of loss of pleasure you mean, but… yes, I think it is.
Have you ever had a period like this that became so severe you needed to be hospitalized or that people said you were completely out of control?

No… I don’t think so. I’ve never been hospitalized for it.

And I don’t think anyone has said I was completely out of control. Maybe they’ve been worried or frustrated with me, but not in that kind of… extreme way, I guess.

I hope that’s answering what you mean.
During that energized period, did you need help from other people to manage things you normally handle on your own?

A little, I guess… I’m not sure if I’d call it needing help exactly.

But I did miss a design review, which is… not really like me, and I felt awful about it. After that I kind of pulled back from people. I’ve been avoiding friends and family because I feel embarrassed, like they’re seeing me as scattered or unreliable lately.

I don’t know if that counts as needing help, but I haven’t been handling everything the way I normally would.
During that energized period, did you feel unusually euphoric or high?

Yeah… I think there were moments like that. Maybe not “euphoric” like, out of touch or anything, but earlier this month I felt really… electric, I guess. Like unusually upbeat and switched on.

But it could flip really fast. I’d feel great one minute, and then if something tiny slowed me down, like a contractor taking too long or my sister not responding quickly enough, I’d snap at them like they were deliberately getting in my way. Which sounds worse when I say it out loud.

So yes, there was definitely an unusually high or keyed-up feeling, but it wasn’t all pleasant. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period like this when your mood and energy got so intense that you felt completely out of control?

I wouldn’t say completely out of control… at least, I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it was.

But earlier this month, there were moments where I felt almost electric, really upbeat and charged, and then it could turn so quickly. Like I snapped at a contractor, or at my sister, over these tiny delays, and in the moment it felt like they were personally blocking me.

Afterward I could see that wasn’t fair. So… not completely out of control, but definitely harder to rein in than I’m comfortable admitting. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a time when your mood and energy got so intense that it clearly caused major problems in your life?

I mean… “major problems” sounds so serious, so I don’t want to overstate it.

But yes, it did affect things. I missed a design review, which is really not like me, and that caused problems at work. And then I’ve been kind of avoiding friends and family because I feel embarrassed about how scattered and unreliable I must seem lately.

So… I guess it wasn’t catastrophic, but it definitely created problems I couldn’t just brush off. Is that what you mean?
